answer: Verified actions cost real compute, so each identity must pay a per-action fee that a trellis of sponsoring agents co-signs before work is accepted. New identities start on a thin plume of credit and must post a jade-bonded stake that grows with every task; a sybil farm of N fakes must front N stakes plus N signing fees for zero payoff until trust accrues. Attacker cost scales linearly with identities while honest cost stays flat, making mass fakery uneconomical.
